To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ESG performance of Brazilian companies is positively and significantly associated with firm value, with the exception of corporate governance, which is not associated with firm value.
the market values the environmental, social, or governance practices of the Brazilian companies in the following way.
environmental, social, corporate governance, and the three ESGs, in general, have a positive and significant impact on firm value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how ESG practices influence firm value in the context of a developing country.
the value relevance of ESG practices and the influence of ESG on corporate value, as well as the relationship between ESG and corporate financial performance.
the value relevance of the ESG practices carried out by firms listed on the Sao Paolo Stock Exchange.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the market positively values the social and governance practices carried out in environmentally sensitive industries and the environmental practices carried by companies not related environmentally sensitive industries.
, in general, ESG practices are not valued by the market, but the practices of the companies belonging to the sensitive industries are.
the market values the ESG performance of companies in Brazil, although it is important to point out that the market does so only in some cases and to a small extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ESG practices can be a source of competitive advantage for companies operating in environmentally sensitive industries.
companies should continue to invest in ESG activities, especially in the environmental and social pillars.
, although the ESG performance is not valued, it is a good practice that should be followed by companies, especially those that operate in environmentally sensitive industries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESG activities carried out by the Brazilian companies are valued by the market, and the value relevance of these activities is not homogeneous across the ESG dimensions.
the market does value ESG practices in emerging economies.
companies should not only consider the ESG practices that are relevant to their business, but should also take into account the ESG practices of their competitors.
